subject.locality: Oviedo, FL 32765 · Cattail Crossing · Seminole County
subject.summary: A four-bedroom, three-bath block pool home in Cattail Crossing with a remodeled kitchen (new cabinets, quartz counters, stainless appliances), updated baths, new flooring, a new roof this year, and a resurfaced pool, as described by you. This analysis estimates what the home is worth in today's market, recommends a list price, and shows what each pricing choice is likely to net you.

summary_page.label: Seller Summary
summary_page.headline: Priced near the middle of what recent sales support, for the strongest first weeks on the market.
why: The closest Cattail Crossing pool sales, adjusted to your home, center just under where we recommend listing.
The market cooled since early in the year: buyers negotiate again, and most sellers help with buyer costs.
Well-priced renovated pool homes nearby are going under contract fast; overpriced ones are sitting.
summary_page.next_step: Review this plan together, sign the listing agreement, and get the home ready to go live.

recommendation.why: It leaves room for the negotiating that is normal right now, and it presents the home as fairly priced during its first weeks on the market, when buyer attention is highest. The two sales that would support a higher price closed earlier in the year, when mortgage rates were lower and homes sold faster than they do now.

means: Expect to negotiate. Recent buyers nearby paid less than the original asking price after seller-paid costs, and most asked the seller to cover part of their closing costs. Plan for both from the start.

The first three weeks matter most. A new listing gets its biggest wave of showings right away. If it is priced where buyers expect, that wave turns into offers; if not, the home starts to look stale and the price cut comes later, from a weaker position.
Watch the appraisal. A contract well above the supported range would risk a low appraisal and a renegotiation, because the appraiser works from the same sales.

Documentation is worth money. Your updates are the reason this home can sell near the top of the neighborhood. The roof permit and final inspection, and permits for the remodel, turn them from claims into value a buyer and an appraiser can rely on.

comps.intro: We looked at every sale nearby since early in the year and chose the closest matches: Cattail Crossing pool homes of about your size, built in the same era. Each is adjusted for its differences from your home, so it reflects what that home would have sold for if it were yours.
comps.method_note: Seller-paid costs are subtracted from the sale price, since they reduce what the seller actually received. Condition adjustments are based on listing descriptions, not visits, so they are judgment calls.

scatter.heading: Where Your Home Fits in the Neighborhood
scatter.takeaway: The renovated comparable sales sit above the dashed line, and at the recommended price your home sits among them, below the two earlier sales at the top.

bullets: Buyers are negotiating again. In recent months, homes nearby sold further under their original asking price after seller-paid costs and took longer to go under contract than earlier in the year.
Inventory is balanced. More homes are for sale than earlier in the year, and many have already cut their price.
Mortgage rates are up from the earlier sales, so buyers' budgets stretch less than they did then.
Timing. Fewer buyers shop between Thanksgiving and New Year's. Launching in the next few weeks gives the home its best window before the holidays.

pricing.stance_reason: the home's documented updates match the strongest sales, which sit near the middle of the range, so it can hold a middle price even with the price cuts around it.
pricing.intro: Three realistic options. Expected sale prices and timelines are our estimates from recent sales. The nets are close, so the real difference between them is time and risk.
pricing.note: The competing-offer option assumes a smaller seller credit, because competing offers usually ask for less help; if they don't show up, its net falls to about the others' level or below.

prep.intro: These steps cost little and remove the questions that slow Florida buyers down or cost sellers money at the negotiating table.

items.detail: Have the permit, final inspection, and any roofer's warranty ready to share. Roof age decides whether a buyer can insure the home, so a documented new roof is one of the most valuable facts in the listing.
items.short: Permit, final inspection and warranty, ready to share

items.detail: A pre-listing inspection plus four-point and wind-mitigation reports. Buyers can get insurance quotes before they offer, and you learn about any issue before a buyer uses it to renegotiate. A new roof usually earns new wind-mitigation credits.
Kitchen, bath, electrical, and plumbing work. Unpermitted work can surface during the buyer's due diligence and delay or derail a sale.
Make sure the property appraiser's record matches the bedrooms and full baths we will advertise.
items.short: The county record matches what we advertise

items.detail: Most recent sales included one. A credit toward a temporary rate buydown lowers a buyer's payment far more in the first years than the same amount off the price.
items.short: Decide it now, before offers arrive

items.detail: If there are steady showings but no offer after the first few weeks, we revisit the price with fresh data rather than waiting.
items.short: Steady showings but no offer? Revisit the price

needs: The roof permit, final inspection, and replacement date, plus any roofer's warranty and wind-mitigation report.
The age of the AC, water heater, and pool equipment, and the dates of the kitchen, bath, flooring, and pool resurfacing work.
Any wind-mitigation features added since the home was built, such as impact windows or storm shutters. They lower a buyer's insurance quote.
Copies of any permits for the remodel work.
Anything you know that affects the home's value or condition, such as past leaks, insurance claims, or repairs. Florida law requires sellers to disclose known material defects.
Your estimated mortgage payoff, so we can turn the net estimates into cash at closing.
When you would like to close, and how you would like showings to work.
sources: the property details and current tax bill you provided
